data.internal-build-and-run#Internal build an:
Once you’ve created your graph, you should test it before launching to the web. To do this, enter “Deliver“ section of the app by pressing the corresponding button in the bottom bar.The section consists of five main columns:
‘New build’ lets you set up a build of your bot. Enter the build name, select a messenger interface and a build preset - a set of rules that will apply to this build. Then press the ‘Build‘ button.
‘Existing builds’ shows a list of your previous builds and the queue of currently processing builds. You can click on an item to see the selected build’s details. An icon on the right hand side represents the status of the build: a green checkmark means that the build has completed successfully, and a red cross means that something went wrong in the process. You can rebuild any of them if the dialogue graph has changed and your preferences for build options have not.
‘New run’ lets you configure a run for a successful build. Enter a name for this run, select a build and a run preset, then press the ‘Run‘ button.
‘Running‘ column shows all the runs that are active right now. You can create different runs for different builds at the same time and compare their performances.
‘Previous runs‘ shows all the runs that have been stopped. All the failed runs will appear in the corresponding section, and both failed and previous runs can be queued for a rerun with an circle arrows button on the right hand side.
data.quick-build--run#Quick build & run: If you don’t want to spend time configuring build and run, you can press ‘Quick build & run‘ button to get the job done automatically. The same set of information will appear once it is complete.
data.test-panel#Test panel: You can also access the test panel to run some additional processes, such as tests and auxiliary runs.
data.launch-to-telegram#Launch to Telegram: As versatile as the internal delivery system is, the point of Chatsky UI is to launch your bots to messengers of your choice.You can do this by pressing “Project menu“ button in the left hand side of the top bar and then selecting “Launch“ option. Choose your preferred messenger, and the instructions in the launch window will lead your way.
data.version-history#Version history: It is recommended to save your graph to version history once in a while. To do this, press the clock icon in the top bar to access history panel. Then enter this version’s name and press ‘Save‘.To load a saved version, open the history panel, select an item and press ‘Restore‘. This will delete your current dialogue graph, so don’t forget to also save it.

data:
Chatsky UI is a web application for creating highly customizable chatbots. This app is based on step-by-step design of the dialog flow, where you define each bot response and predict what the end user may reply. The result is a dialog graph in which all dialog variants are specified. You can assign bot responses and possible user reactions in a variety of ways: direct quotes, simplified intent-based constructions, LLM prompts, and Python code.To make your bot more personalized, you can also define slots - pieces of information about a user that can be utilized in a conversation, such as the person's name, phone number or email, as well as data relevant to the conversation, such as their favorite hobby or a product they're interested in.For further convenience and versatility, you can import vocabularies, create your own code snippets and small parts of a dialog flow which will be available in the dedicated library, right at your fingertips.Flexible settings also allow you to customize the bot for your needs. You can configure the pipeline in which you can connect additional dialog context processing services, add presets for building the bot after its configuration, and connect third-party LLM services for processing prompts.If you do not want to manually enter all the branches of the dialog, you can import or create your own dialog samples, based on which the program will build a dialog graph. All you have to do now is configure the bot for optimal performance.After you have created, built and run your bot, you can chat with it in the internal dialog interface or directly in a messenger, and the logs of the build, run and additional tests will help you understand where the error could occur.
You can explore the layout of Chatsky UI in the following sections.
data.homepage#Homepage:
The homepage shows the skill you are working on, as well as all the flows within.The list of available actions with the skill:
Rename your project and change its description
Open Chatsky code for this skill
Download a local copy of the project
Share the project for collaboration
Delete the project
The list of available actions with flows:
Rename and change the description
Open flow settings
Rearrange flows
Also on this screen you can access the app settings.
data.editor#Editor:
Editor is the main workspace of Chatsky UI. This is where you create a skill, test it, build and run it, and eventually launch it in messengers.
All the editor components will be further explained down below
data.project-menu#Project menu: The project menu provides access to essential editing functions, including undo and redo, as well as the ability to save the project and download a local copy. Additionally, it offers the option to launch your bot to Telegram.
data.user-menu#User menu:
The account menu currently contains only three options:
Switch color themes
Shortcuts panel
Help center link
Account settings will be added with an upcoming release.
data.tabs#Tabs:
The bottom panel is the navigation within Chatsky UI.The left mouse button with Chatsky UI logo leads to the homepage.
The left mouse button with Chatsky UI logo leads to the homepage.
The middle section consists of five tabs
data.import#Import: Import tab allows you to upload or create dialog samples, assign flows and convert them into the first draft of your skill.
data.edit#Edit: Edit tab is the main canvas of Chatsky UI, on which nodes are located. The left panel contains the list of flows, as well as the components available for use - nodes, links, slots and presets you have created.Quick build and run option is also currently located at the top bar of Edit screen. This is a temporary solution before Deliver tab is released.
data.deliver#Deliver: Deliver tab allows you to set up your bot’s build and run configurations. After the bot is run, you will be able to test it in the internal chat panel or launch it to messengers.Read more about build & run.
data.inspect#Inspect: Inspect is the panel where all the build and run, as well as internal test logs are displayed. You can review errors, backtrack successful builds and chat with your bot in this tab.Read more about Inspect.
data.settings#Settings: Settings tab allows you to configure general settings, as well as the pipeline, build & run and advanced settings.Read more about Settings.
data.library#Library: Library is the general collection of all components that you have created or uploaded that can be used when creating and editing a skill. Library contains all the code components, conditions, responses, slot snippets, presets, intents and vocabulary items you may need in your work.Read more about Library.
data.notifications#Notifications: The bottom panel also contains notifications menu. You can configure notifications in ‘Settings → Advanced’.

data: Inspect section of the app allows you to troubleshoot any issue with your bot. This is the place where you can test the bot in action by chatting with it and inspect all its builds and runs’ logs.
data.logs#Logs: Every action you take in ‘Deliver’ section is recorded in logs under a corresponding name. You can select a build, a run or a test you have conducted and see if they were successful, and if not, what went wrong.
data.build-logs#Build logs: Build logs page consists of build’s status, completion time, duration, chosen preset and logs themself which you can inspect in Chatsky UI or export by clicking a link.
data.chat-preview#Chat preview:
Chat window in Chatsky UI imitates your preferred messenger interface and changes its functionality depending on what interface you have chosen for every particular build.
Note that different messengers come with different features. For example, button conditions are available only on Telegram and will not be shown if your build is for WhatsApp.
data.select-chat#Select chat: After you have built and run your bot, expand the chat window by pressing << button, then click New chat and select a build and a run, then you can chat with it.Chat history is saved in the panel’s sidebar, so you can test several chats all at once.
data.refresh-dialog#Refresh dialog: If you want to start over and chat with your bot from the beginning, simply press the ‘Refresh‘ button.
data.select-messenger-interface#Select messen: If you have used Quick build and run option or have not specified any messenger interface, your build will be suitable for all of them. To test your bot in different interfaces, select one in the top bar of the chat window.
data.more-options#More options:
Pressing three dots at the top right corner of the chat window reveals two more options for chat management:
Export dialog history to share it with your team members or for a future Chatsky UI project
Restore an old build version if you like that chat best

data.system-requirements#System requirements: Ensure you have Python version 3.9 or higher installed (Excluding 3.9.7).
data.local-installation#Local installation:
To install the package and necessary dependencies, run the following command:
pip install chatsky-ui
data.chatsky-ui-app-configuration#Chatsky UI:
You may add a .env file in the root directory and configure any of following environment variables. The values shown below are the default ones.
HOST=0.0.0.0
PORT=8000
CONF_RELOAD=False
LOG_LEVEL=info
GRACEFUL_TERMINATION_TIMEOUT=2  # Waiting for process to stop
PING_PONG_TIMEOUT=0.5  # Waiting the process to response before it mark it as still `running`
# For tests:
BUILD_COMPLETION_TIMEOUT=10
RUN_RUNNING_TIMEOUT=5
The chatsky.ui init command will start an interactive cookiecutter process to create a project based on a predefined template. The resulting project will be a simple example template that you can customize to suit your needs.
data.run-your-project#Run your project:
To start your project, use the following command:
chatsky.ui run_app --project-dir <PROJECT-SLUG>  # Replace <PROJECT-SLUG> with the slug you specified during initialization
data.documentation#Documentation: You can refer to the documentation to dig into the application code understanding.

data: Default node represents the state of the dialogue at the moment - the current bot response and all possible user replies (conditions) with the following transitions to other nodes.You can see the default node on the image (Coming soon). The node name is placed at the top and is created only for your convenience. The responsе is located below, and all user replies - conditions - are located below it.
data.response#Response: During the response configuration process, you enter the name of the response and select one of the three types of responses available in Chatsky UI:
data.prompt#Prompt:
You can configure the response using the LLM prompt. This way, the bot's response will be unique every time and will be able to repeat the sentiment you need for the dialogue.The view of the response configuration with the prompt is shown below. It consists of:
the title that you will see on the node
selection of the LLM model that will process the prompt
prompt itself
You can also test the prompt. To do this, click the ‘Test prompt’ button and in the menu that opens, click the ‘Run’ button.
data.python#Python:
Python response is the most versatile way to create a bot response, but requires the ability to work with code.During the setup process, you need to set:
response title
Python code itself
You can also highlight individual code snippets and save them as components. These components will be available from the library.
data.quote#Quote: This is the simplest, but also the least versatile way to create a reponse. Just write the name of the response and a quote that the bot will send to the user in every dialogue cycle.
data.condition#Condition: Condition in Chatsky UI is an expectation of what an end user might say. If the condition is satisfied, dialog transitions to the according node.Conditions can be configured in a number of ways:
data.prompt-1#Prompt:
Similarly to responses, you can describe a condition with a prompt using an LLM.Modal window structure:
condition title that will show on the node
model name and API key. If you have your LLM services configured in the settings, your default model and its API key will show
prompt itself
condition satisfaction triggers
Read more about prompt engineering in Chatsky UI.You can also test your prompt before saving the condition. Click on the 'Test prompt' button, enter a sample user message and click 'Run'. The status message below will show if the condition has been satisfied.
data.basic#Basic:
Basic conditions are designed for beginners and include only the simplest ways of configuring a condition. Condition title in this case is purely optional, however it helps distinguish the conditions you have created in the long run.There are six structures of basic conditions:
Exact match: if user’s message fully matches the text in the box, only then the condition is satisfied
Include text: if user’s message includes the text in the box, the condition is satisfied
Regular expression: if the message matches the regexp structure in the box, the condition is satisfied
Any of: this structure allows you to configure several ways in which the condition is satisfied. After selecting ‘any of’, you can add any number of basic conditions, only one of which has to be triggered to satisfy the condition
All of: similarly, after selecting this option, you can add any number of basic conditions, all of which have to be triggered to satisfy the condition
Not: this structure just adds negation of the following basic condition
data.slots#Slots: This condition type can be satisfied if user sends a message that contains the chosen slot.To use slot condition, you need to first create a Slots node. Then, to configure the condition, select a flow containing the slots node, a group and a specific slot.
data.button#Button:
Button condition can only be used in Telegram messenger interface. It replaces entering a message manually with a set of buttons which can be helpful for bots with linear structure.There are three types of button conditions:
Inline button which sticks to its message bubble
Large sticky button
Command which shows on top of the text field and always starts with the slash: /command
Learn how to set up messenger interfaces in Chatsky UI.
data.python-1#Python:
Python code is the most versatile type of conditions, but requires the ability to work with code.During the setup process, you need to set:
condition title
Python code itself
You can also highlight individual code snippets and save them as components. These components will be available from the library.
data.intents#Intents: Intents condition allows you to select any number of intents which can be found in user’s message. To use this type of condition, you first need to upload intents to the library.Then you can enter or select from the list below the intents, all of which have to be triggered to satisfy the condition. Separate the intents in the box using the 'Enter' key.
data.default-node-settings#Default node setti: Press the settings button next to the node name to configure your nodes even further.In the settings window you can rename your node, enter its response window, set conditions’ priorities and even rearrange conditions list by dragging them up and down.
data.transitions#Transitions:
Every default node has to be connected to another one to work. Transitions work as such: a condition triggered in one node leads to a response in another node. To achieve this, select a condition in the first node that has to be triggered, find the orange circle in the right hand side and drag it to the blue circle in the second node’s response.Note that a condition has to be linked to a single response, however different conditions can be linked to a single response.There also are transition functions that allow you create connections not dependant on physical links between two nodes, but on functions that analyze following nodes and previous ones, so that if you rearrange them or change completely, the pattern will stay the same.Here is the list of all transition functions:
Forward - transitions to the next node in the queue
Backward - transitions to the backward node in the queue
Previous - transitions to the previous node in the queue
Current - transitions one node’s condition to its own response
To start - transitions to the start node
To fallback - transitions to the fallback node
To apply a transition function, instead of dragging an orange circle next to a condition, click on it and a small window with all the functions will appear.In order to make some of the functions work properly, you should check your graph using the list view. It shows every node of your flow as a list, the default order of which is chronological, based on when you have created every node.You can access the list view by pressing the list button in the top bar of the Edit page. This view shows not only simple transitions, but also every function’s destination. If you want to rearrange some of your nodes, simply drag them up or down and drop where you prefer. All the transition functions will adjust automatically.

data:
Nodes are the core elements of your skill. With their help, most of the skill configuration takes place - from creating dialogue lines to extracting necessary information from user's messages.
The following pages describe each type of node.

After connecting every node within a flow, you should place transitions across between all other flows. To do this, use link - a node-like structure that executes the same transition as an arrow but across two flows.In the first flow, select ‘Link’ in the sidebar and drag it onto the canvas. A modal window will show up automatically. Select a flow, to which you would like to transition, and a node - the destination point. After that, connect any node to the link with an arrow. Now, the arrow-connected node is the "from" and the node you have selected in the window is the "to".
data.list-of-incoming-links#List of incoming: If you go to the second flow, the "to" node now has an indicator showing incoming links. You can click on it and review all the transitions from different flows.

data:
If you have a configuration of several nodes that you would like to use multiple times in your projects, you can create presets and drag them onto canvas just like any other component.
Select every node you need by dragging left mouse button across the canvas or by clicking on every node while pressing Shift key
Click on the jigsaw icon in the top bar, and 'New preset' modal window will appear
Enter preset name, select a display color and click 'Create'
Your preset will be stored in the 'Presets' section of the sidebar
Presets save nodes with everything you have configured inside previously. You can access and review your presets in the according Library section.

Slots are a tool that helps you make your bot feel more personal. They let you configure which pieces of information the bot can remember and use in the dialogue later. For example, if a user enters their name during a conversation, the bot can remember it and say it when it is appropriate.The tutorial below explain what kinds of slots are available in Chatsky UI and how to configure them.
data.slot-types#Slot types:
Slots are essentially pieces of text that can be extracted and then placed into bot's responses. There are two extraction methods:
LLM prompt - enter a prompt describing what piece of information this slot has to remember
Regular expression - if the text you would like to extract is unique to this message, enter a regexp structure describing that text
Read more on regepx syntax.
data.slots-node#Slots node: Slots in Chatsky UI are stored and created in slots nodes. You can find this component in the sidebar alongside default node.
data.slot-group#Slot group: After dragging a slots node to the canvas, you can create a slot group inside it. A group unites several slots based on any attribute you like. For example, user's name and their age will go perfectly in 'Personal info' group. After creating a group, you can create individual slots inside it using methods discussed above.You can access every group by pressing arrow button next to it. Here you can configure all the slots inside the group and set, whether this group is standalone or a subgroup of another one. Subgroups are rendered inside their parent groups in the slots node.
data.slots-node-settings#Slots node settings: Nodes settings are a modal window that you can access by pressing a 'Settings' button on the slots node. This window shows the node's description and all the groups inside it. Here you can create new groups reorder them by dragging three lines on the left hand side in the table.

data: This is a quick start tutorial
data.global-flow#Global flow: Global flow is the place for configuring nodes and slots that are ubiquitous for every other flow. It comes with a preset Global node that does not have any response and cannot be connected to any other node but the conditions you create will be added to every node in the graph.If you would like to have a set of slots that will be filled and used across the whole dialog, create Slots node in the global flow.Read more about flows
data.local-nodes#Local nodes: Local node has the same purpose as the global node but has effect only in the flow it is placed in. All local conditions created in this node will appear in every other node in the flow.
data.start-node#Start node:
Start node represents the state that occurs in the beginning of a dialogue. After activating bot, it texts you the first response and then the dialogue thread unravels. You have to manually assign start node by selecting a preferred node and pressing the green play button ▶️ in the top bar. Selecting another node and repeating the process will transfer ‘start’ property to a new node.
Note, that there can be only one start node for the whole graph.
data.fallback-node#Fallback node: Fallback node is the dialogue state that occurs when no conditions in the current node were triggered. You should assign ‘fallback‘ property to a node that is significant to the dialogue, so your user will not be confused. Fallback node can also have a response explaining that the dialogue is stalled, such as: “Sorry, I didn’t get it. What would you like to talk about?“Fallback node acts just like start node: there can also be only one and th assign it you select a node and press red repeat button ↶ in the top bar.
data.flows#Flows:
Once you’ve configured global node, you can move to creating a set of flows necessary to your bot.
Press the plus button + next to the “Flows“ title in the sidebar
Enter a flow name, a short description and select a color that will represent this flow in the modal window
Press “Create“ button below
The flow will appear in the sidebar below Global flow.Repeat the process for every other flow.
data.graph#Graph:
Your dialogue graph is built out of nodes, so to create the first one:
Expand the “Nodes“ section of the sidebar
Drag “Default node“ and drop it on the canvas
Press the section of the node with the robot icon - it represents this node’s response
Configure the response in the modal window and press “Save“
Add the first condition by pressing plus button + on the node
Configure the condition and press “Save“
Create the rest of conditions
Now that you have the first node, create the second one. To connect them, select a condition in the first node that has to be triggered to transition to the next node, find the orange circle in the right hand side and drag it to the blue circle in the second node.
data.links#Links: Once you’ve created your first flow’s graph, you can move to configuring another flow.To connect the flows, you should first create a node in the second one. Then move back to the first flow and drag and drop “Link” node to the canvas. A modal window will show up, in which you configure its endpoint: select the second flow and a node in there.This link now represents the corresponding node, and you can connect them by dragging a transition just like between two nodes.
data.build-and-run#Build and run: Once you’ve created your graph, you should test it before launching to the web. To do this, enter “Deliver“ section of the app by pressing the corresponding button in the bottom bar.Deliver section offers you thorough control over your builds and runs. You can read more on that later.Press “Quick build & run“ button to get your bot ready to chat. It will take no more than a minute depending on your hardware.
data.testing-and-troubleshooting#Testing and: To enter chat, move to “Inspect“ section by pressing the corresponding button in the bottom bar.This section shows you build and run logs, and if any of the sidebar’s items show red cross next to build or run, this mean that an error had occurred, and you have to solve it and rerun the bot.If the Inspect sidebar shows successful build and run, you can chat with your bot in the window next to logs. Chatting with the bot several cycles will reveal any errors you might have done while creating the graph.
data.launch#Launch: Once you are happy with the dialogue process, you can launch your bot to a messenger you prefer.To do this, press “Project menu“ button in the left hand side of the top bar, then press “Launch“. Select your preferred messenger, and the instructions in the launch window will lead your way.

data: Settings in Chatsky UI are an essential component of configuring your bot. Settings are divided into five sections, every one of which are explained below.
data.general#General:
General settings allow you to customize Chatsky UI’s appearance according to your preferences. Here you can switch themes and change UI language.List of supported languages:
English
Russian (coming soon)

data: A skill is the course of the whole dialog with all the variants of its development that can occur while talking to your bot. In Chatsky UI, a skill consists of flows, essentially conversation topics, into which a skill is divided to simplify working on it. Each flow consists of nodes that represent current state of the bot along with all possible transitions to other nodes.We will look at each element of the skill in detail below.
data.flows#Flows: A flow is the part of the skill in which a conversation with the bot on one specific topic takes place. For example, all branches of dialog on the topic of traveling should be placed in a 'Travel' flow.
data.flow-list#Flow list: The list of your flows is located in the left sidebar. Each flow has a name, a short description and a color label for easier navigation among them. You will also find there a search bar for flows and other components, a button for creating a new flow and a button for managing existing flows.
data.create-a-new-flow#Create a new flow: You can create a new flow by pressing ‘+‘ button in the sidebar. To configure the flow, enter its name, no shorter than two characters, a short description, and select a preferred color label.
data.manage-and-edit-your-flows#Manage and ed: Pressing ‘Manage flows‘ button reveals a modal window where you can configure all your flows after you have created them. You can access all the same settings as in the ‘New flow’ window and reorder them.
data.nodes#Nodes: Nodes are the core elements of your skill. A default node represents a state of the dialog, in which the bot has sent a message, and the user is yet to reply to it.The in-depth explanation of nodes is available in the corresponding section.
